## How to review

1. Verses: do the listed ayat really contain what each claim says? Is any claim stronger than its ayat?
2. Pronouns and speakers: where the Arabic names none, does the draft say so?
3. Words with more than one reading: decide how the page words each.
4. Omissions: anything the verses say that readers need and the chapter leaves out?
5. No added facts: no name, number, place, reason, emotion or sequence beyond the ayat; no implied chronology.
6. No depiction of any prophet, angel or jinn.
7. Theology and etiquette: cautious wording about prophets; no verdicts; no legal or medical ruling.
8. Kids mode only restates the claims; nothing frightening or misleading.
9. Lessons are marked as interpretation and are modest; none reads as scripture or a promise.
10. Unknowns and tradition: each 'Named in later tradition' line is accurate and only a label.
11. Titles and honorifics: bare names in the draft; honorifics added at render time.
12. Sign-off goes in the platform review flow (name, version, decision), not in this file.

## 1. The request and the birds  (`#the-request-and-the-birds`)

Cited ayat: 2:260

> **2:260** وَإِذْ قَالَ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّ أَرِنِى كَيْفَ تُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰ قَالَ أَوَلَمْ تُؤْمِن قَالَ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِن لِّيَطْمَئِنَّ قَلْبِى قَالَ فَخُذْ أَرْبَعَةً مِّنَ ٱلطَّيْرِ فَصُرْهُنَّ إِلَيْكَ ثُمَّ ٱجْعَلْ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ جَبَلٍ مِّنْهُنَّ جُزْءًا ثُمَّ ٱدْعُهُنَّ يَأْتِينَكَ سَعْيًا وَٱعْلَمْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ

### Claims

**c1** (2:260): The one who speaks in the passage asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead.

**c2** (2:260): God asked whether he did not believe, and he answered yes, but that his heart might be at ease.

**c3** (2:260): God told him to take four of the birds and to incline them to himself, the Arabic being read in more than one way.

**c4** (2:260): Then he was to place a part of them on every mountain.

**c5** (2:260): Then he was to call them, and they would come to him hastening.

**c6** (2:260): God told him to know that God is Almighty and Wise.

### One-minute summary

The one who speaks in the passage asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead [c1]. God told him to take four birds and to call them, and they would come to him hastening [c3][c5].

### Complete story

The one who speaks in the passage asked his Lord to show him how He gives life to the dead [c1]. God asked whether he did not believe, and he answered yes, but that his heart might be at ease [c2].

God told him to take four of the birds and to incline them to himself [c3]. Then he was to place a part of them on every mountain [c4], and then to call them, and they would come to him hastening [c5]. God told him to know that God is Almighty and Wise [c6].

### Deep study

The passage is a short exchange in which a request [c1] is met by a question and an answer [c2], and then by an instruction in steps [c3][c4][c5]. The instruction ends with a reminder of God's might and wisdom [c6]. The Arabic of the first step, rendered 'incline them to yourself', is read in more than one way [c3].

### Kids mode

A servant of God asked Him to show how He gives life to the dead [c1]. God told him to take four birds and to call them, and they would come to him [c3][c5].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the speaker says belief and a heart at ease are not the same thing, and God does not rebuke the request [c2]. Another is that the passage ends by naming God as Almighty and Wise [c6].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: which birds, where, or when; the verse says only four of the birds.
- The Arabic phrase in the first step is read in more than one way (to incline them to yourself, or to cut them up); the verse does not decide, and a scholar should word it.
- Not established: what happened to the birds after the call beyond that they come hastening; the verse does not describe it.
- Not established: what it means that the parts were placed on every mountain, or how many mountains.
- The verse does not say what prompted the request.
